sentences.text: 1. The insurer is in appeal being aggrieved by the finding of the Tribunal that the vehicle that had insured was involved in the accident and consequently contending that they would not be liable to pay any compensation.
sentences._hearing_file: The Manager vs Nagamma on 11 November, 2024.json

sentences.text: 2. The principal argument of the insurer is that the medical records which were relied upon by the claimant indicated that she suffered a road traffic accident, but the vehicle that was involved was not mentioned in the hospital records.
sentences._hearing_file: The Manager vs Nagamma on 11 November, 2024.json

sentences.text: The principal NC: 2024:KHC:45630 contention of the insurer that the hospital records did not indicate with which vehicle the two wheeler (in which the claimant was riding pillion) collided with and the records did not indicate the registration number of the vehicle at all.
sentences._hearing_file: The Manager vs Nagamma on 11 November, 2024.json

sentences.text: It is contended that the complaint was lodged nine days after the incident, at which point in time the vehicle number was mentioned and therefore this was a clear case of the vehicle being implicated in the accident.
sentences._hearing_file: The Manager vs Nagamma on 11 November, 2024.json

sentences.text: 3. The hospital records which are produced indicate that the claimant was brought to the hospital with the history of a road traffic accident while she was riding pillion.
sentences._hearing_file: The Manager vs Nagamma on 11 November, 2024.json

sentences.text: It is no doubt true that in these medical records the vehicle with which the two wheeler met with an accident is not mentioned.
sentences._hearing_file: The Manager vs Nagamma on 11 November, 2024.json

sentences.text: However, the argument of the insurer would fail into insignificance in the light of the suggestion made by its own counsel to the claimant on 14.08.2017.
sentences._hearing_file: The Manager vs Nagamma on 11 November, 2024.json
